newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Arab-Malaysian group to review structure - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Malaysian group to review structure - chairman.

text.p: The Arab-Malaysian group, one of Malaysia's biggest finance houses is to review its organisational structure, group chairman Azman Hashim said.
"We will be looking into our group structure (to see) whether there is any better way of doing our business," he told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
The aim was to "reorganise ourselves; it is an ongoing exercise", he said.
The restructuring was required as a lot of changes were taking place in the Malaysian financial sector, Azman added.

"Lots of changes are going on with big banks coming in with big mergers. We are facing more big boys than before and they are not foreigners, they are locals. At the same time along the horizon, we could be facing foreigners, too," he said.
Under pressure from Bank Negara Malaysia, the central bank, several commercial banks have been seeking mergers and raising capital before the country is opened to more competition.
This year, after taking over United Malayan Banking Corp Bhd (UMBC), now renamed Sime bank, Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby, has announced plans to acquire a majority stake in Oriental Bank Bhd.
Recently, stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd announced a deal to acquire Kwong Yik Bank and merge it with its associate DCB Holdings Bhd's banking unit, to create the third-biggest bank in the country.
Bank of Commerce, part of Commerce Asset Holdings Bhd, is in the market to raise 1.2 billion ringgit, which has fuelled speculation about a possible merger with another bank.
On Thursday, Singapore-based United Overseas Bank, announced it would merge its two Malaysian units United Overseas Bank (M) Bhd and Chung Khiaw Bank (M) Bhd.

"There are a lot of challenges ahead ... We may have to look for more smart partnerships with other people (who have) the right expertise from overseas ... to strengthen ourselves to compete with the best," Azman said.
